checks.note: Class-level @Transactional on AuthService has no noRollbackFor; recordAttempt (private, unannotated) saves the LoginAttempt and both callers in login() then throw BadCredentialsException (a RuntimeException) from the same transaction, rolling back the insert. Verification caveat checked: no REQUIRES_NEW or noRollbackFor on any shown path into loginAttemptRepository.save, so countByIdentifierAndAttemptedAtAfter never sees failed attempts and the lockout cannot engage.

AuthService.logout filters on !t.isUsed() and only touches the presented token; markAllUsedByUserId is called only from refresh's theft branches, never from logout, so a refresh that commits first leaves its successor token (newRt, used=false, full TTL) valid after logout. The opposite interleaving also fails as described: RefreshToken is @Version-ed (refresh catches ObjectOptimisticLockingFailureException), so logout's save errors and revokes nothing. Frontend Promise.race overlap could not be checked (no file tools), but the server-side revocation gap is fully shown in this file.

routes.js confirms the player-subscription route (name 'player-subscription', ~line 203) uses meta `requiresParent: true` instead of `role: 'PARENT'`, but whether that key is ignored depends on router/index.js, which is not shown — and the heavy use of `requiresCoach: true` on coach routes suggests the guard may handle `requires*` keys, contradicting the finding's claim. The finding's own verification caveat (backend authorization of the subscription endpoints) is also unverifiable from this file.
